αἰθούσῃ: αἴθουσα — portico, colonnaded hall; fem. dat. sg.

αὖτ: αὖτε (elided αὖτ’) — again, in turn, moreover; epic adv./conj.

δέσποινα: δέσποινα — mistress, lady of the house; fem. nom. sg.

δῖος: δῖος — heavenly, divine, illustrious; masc. nom. sg., epithet of heroes (= fem. δῖα)

δῶμα: δῶμα — house, hall, dwelling; acc. sg.

κέλευθον: κέλευθος — way, path, journey; fem. acc. sg.
κήδε: κῆδος — care, sorrow, trouble; neut. acc. pl., elided (κήδε’ = κήδεα, uncontracted; Attic κήδη)

κε: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν)

κούρην: κούρη — girl, daughter (epic = Attic κόρη); fem. acc. sg.
κοῦροι: κοῦρος — young man, boy; nom. pl.
κτήματα: κτῆμα — possession, property; neut. nom./acc. pl.

κῦμα: κῦμα — wave; nom. sg. · also acc. sg. (identical neut. form), object of a preposition (κατὰ κῦμα ’over the wave’) · also acc. sg., direct object: μέγα κῦμα ’a great wave’
λέκτο: λέγω — count, reckon; aor. mid. 3 sg.: ’he counted’ · also λέχομαι — lie down to rest; aor. mid. 3 sg.: ’he lay down’ — the identical forms of two different verbs are a deliberate wordplay
λέχος: λέχος — bed, couch; neut. nom./acc. sg.
λαῖτμα: λαῖτμα — the gulf, the deep (of the sea); neut. nom./acc. sg.

λεχέεσσιν: λέχος — bed, couch; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσι, plural for a single bed
λεῖος: λεῖος — smooth; adj., masc. nom. sg., + gen. of separation: ’free of, smooth of’
λιαρόν: λιαρός — warm, mild; masc./neut. acc. sg.

μάλα: μάλα — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.

νεώτερον: νέος — young; comparative νεώτερος, masc. acc. sg.
νῆα: ναῦς — ship; acc. sg., epic νῆα

ξανθὸν: ξανθός — yellow, tawny, fair (of hair); masc. acc. sg.
ξεῖν: ξεῖνος — stranger, guest-friend; voc. sg., elided (ξεῖν’ = ξεῖνε)

οὔτε: οὔτε — nor, and not; correlative negative conj.

σὴν: σός — your, yours; fem. acc. sg.
σὺ: σύ — you (sg.); nom. sg. (grave, mid-clause form)
σὺν: σύν — with, together with; prep. + dat. · also as adverb, ’together’, or as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb: σὺν … κάλυψε = συνεκάλυψε ’covered up’; σὺν … ἔπεσον = συνέπεσον ’fell together, clashed’
σῖτον: σῖτος — bread, grain, the staple of a meal; acc. sg.
τ: τε (elided τ’) — and; ’epic τε’ also marks a standing fact · after οὔ νυ perhaps τοι ’to you’ · also in a question, an expressive epic τε with no connective force, giving a note of doubt or wonder (πῶς τε ...; ’how, pray...?’)
τά: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl.; also relative: ’which’ (accented τά before a following enclitic)
τάδε: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’
τάπητας: τάπης — carpet, rug; masc. acc. pl.
τήν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg., resumptive: ’whom’ · also demonstrative, fem. acc. sg., resuming an earlier noun: ’her’ (τήν … ῥέξω ’her I will sacrifice’)
ταῦτά: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’, accented before an enclitic
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τετιημένος: τετίημαι — be grieved, be downcast (defective, perf. with pres. force); perf. part. masc. nom. sg.
τι: τις, τι — someone, something; neut. acc. sg., used adverbially with negatives ’at all’ · also adjectival indefinite: ’some, any’ (τι δήμιον ἄλλο ’some other public matter’) · also adverbial without a negative: ’in some way, in some measure’ (τι κατὰ πρῆξιν ’on some business’) · also as a substantive object, in a question: ’anything, something’ (ἦ ῥά τι ἴδμεν ’do we know anything’) · also the neut. of τις forming, with a preceding ὅ, the indefinite relative ὅ τι ’whatever, that which’ (αὔδα ὅ τι φρονέεις ’say whatever you have in mind’)
τις: τις, τι — someone, something, a certain one; indefinite pron., masc./fem. nom. sg.
τοι: σύ — you (sg.); encl. dat. sg.: ’to/for you’ · also τοι, the affirming particle: ’you know, indeed’ (esp. in ἦ τοι, οὔ τοι); the two are not always easy to keep apart
τοιαῦτα: τοιοῦτος — such, of such a kind; demonstr. pron./adj., neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’such things’
τοιοῦτον: τοιοῦτος — such, of this kind; masc. acc. sg.
τοῖος: τοῖος — such, of such a kind; masc. nom. sg. (τοῖος ... οἷον ’such as’)
τοῦ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. gen. sg. ’of him, that one’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whose, of whom; masc. gen. sg. (τοῦ νῶι θεοῦ ὣς τερπόμεθ’ αὐδῇ ’whose voice we delight in’) · also demonstrative gen. of comparison after a comparative: τοῦ γε κρεῖσσον ’better than this’
τοῦτο: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. nom./acc. sg.
τοῦτό: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. nom./acc. sg., accented before enclitic γ’
τρητοῖς: τρητός — bored, pierced (with holes for cords); masc./neut. dat. pl.
τόδ: ὅδε — this, this here; neut. nom./acc. sg., elided (τόδ’ = τόδε)
τόδε: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., neut. nom./acc. sg.
τότε: τότε — then, at that time; adv.
τὴν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg. ’her’ · also ’it’, of a thing (τὴν = the clothing): fem. acc. sg. · also with a noun, article-like: τὴν ὁδόν ’that journey’
τὸν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg. ’him’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom, which; masc. acc. sg. (τὸν Ἀλφειὸς τέκε ’whom Alpheus begot’) · also demonstrative adjective with a noun: ’that, the’ (τὸν μῦθον ’that story, message’)
τῆμος: τῆμος — then, at that time; correlative temporal adv. answering ἦμος ’when’
τῇ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. dat. sg.: ’her, with her’ · also adverbial, ’there, in that place’, pointing back to a place just named (τῇ τόν γε μένον λοχόωντες ’there they lay in wait for him’) · also relative, fem. dat. sg., serving as an instrumental, ’with which’ (ῥάβδον, τῇ τ’ ἀνδρῶν ὄμματα θέλγει ’a wand, with which he charms men’s eyes’), not the personal pronoun
τῷ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc./neut. dat. sg.; also relative: ’in which’ · the relative dat. sg. also serves as an instrumental, ’with which’ (τῷ δάμνησι ’with which she overpowers’) · also adverbial ’therefore, and so’ (τῷ οὔ τινα οἶδα ’so I know no one’)
φάν: φημί — say, speak; aor. 3 pl., unaugmented, contracted (φάν = φάσαν/ἔφασαν): ’they said’
φάσ: φημί — say, assert; pres. 3 pl., elided (φάσ’ = φασί): ’they say’
φάτο: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented (= ἔφατο)
φέρεσθαι: φέρω — carry; mid. pres. inf.: ’to carry off for oneself’ · also pass. inf., ’to be carried’ (by the wind): Βορέῃ προβάλεσκε φέρεσθαι ’would toss it to the North Wind to be carried’
φέρων: φέρω — carry, bear; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’carrying’
φίλον: φίλος — dear, one’s own (with kin/body parts serves as a possessive); neut. nom./acc. sg. · also masc. acc. sg., agreeing with a masculine noun: φίλον υἱόν ’dear son’ · also masc. acc. sg. predicative, agreeing with a pronoun: ’as a friend, welcome’ (φίλον ἐλθεῖν)
φαιήκων: Φαίηξ — a Phaeacian; masc. gen. pl.
φρεσὶν: φρήν — mind, heart, wits (lit. midriff); fem. dat. pl.
φρονέων: φρονέω — think, intend, be disposed; pres. part. nom. sg. masc., epic uncontracted (= Attic φρονῶν)
φύλλοισι: φύλλον — leaf; neut. dat. pl., epic -οισι
φώνησέν: φωνέω — utter, speak aloud, call out; aor. 3 sg., accented φώνησέν before the enclitic τε
φῦλ: φῦλον — tribe, race, class; neut. acc. pl., elided (φῦλ’ = φῦλα): ‘tribes’
χεῦεν: χέω — pour; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (contrast augmented ἔχευε)
χθονὶ: χθών — earth, ground; fem. dat. sg.
χλαίνας: χλαῖνα — a thick cloak, mantle; fem. acc. pl.
χώρῳ: χῶρος — place, spot; masc. dat. sg.
χῶρος: χῶρος — place, spot; masc. nom. sg.
ἀέκοντα: ἄκων — unwilling; masc. acc. sg., epic ἀέκων (= Attic ἄκοντα): ’against his will’
ἀγήραον: ἀγήραος (= ἀγήρως) — ageless, not growing old; masc./fem. acc. sg., predicate adj. with θήσειν: ’ageless’ (ἀ- + γῆρας)
ἀγορεῦσαι: ἀγορεύω — speak, say, proclaim; aor. inf.: ’to speak, to say’
ἀγόρευον: ἀγορεύω — speak, say, declare; impf. 3 pl.
ἀθάνατον: ἀθάνατος — immortal, deathless; masc./fem. acc. sg.
ἀθηναίη: Ἀθηναίη — Athena; fem. nom. sg., epic full form (= Ἀθήνη)
ἀλκίνοος: Ἀλκίνοος — Alcinous, king of the Phaeacians; nom. sg.
ἀλλήλους: ἀλλήλων — one another; reciprocal pron., masc. acc. pl.
ἀμβροσίη: ἀμβρόσιος — ambrosial, divine, immortal; adj., fem. nom. sg., standing epithet of night
ἀμφιπόλοισι: ἀμφίπολος — handmaid, attendant; fem. dat. pl., epic -οισι
ἀμφιπόλοισιν: ἀμφίπολος — handmaid, attendant; fem. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις)
ἀμφὶ: ἀμφί — on both sides, around, about; prep./adv. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἀμφὶ ... βάλλομεν = ἀμφιβάλλομεν ’we threw around, embraced’)
ἀνέμοιο: ἄνεμος — wind; gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
ἀνείρεαι: ἀνείρομαι — ask, inquire; pres. 2 sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic -ῃ)
ἀνθρώπων: ἄνθρωπος — human being, man; gen. pl.
ἀντιάσαντα: ἀντιάω — meet, meet with, come by (+ gen.); aor. part. masc. acc. sg., agreeing with ἱκέτην: ’one who has met with’
ἀπάνευθε: ἀπάνευθε — far away, apart, at a distance; adv., + gen.
ἀπέφθιθεν: ἀποφθίνω — perish, die; aor. pass. 3 pl., epic short ending -θεν (= Attic ἀπεφθίθησαν): ’perished’
ἀπήμονά: ἀπήμων — without harm (ἀ- + πῆμα): harmless, doing no harm, or unharmed, safe; masc./fem. acc. sg.
ἀπαμειβόμενος: ἀπαμείβομαι — answer, reply; pres. part. nom. sg. masc.
ἀπείρονα: ἀπείρων — boundless, endless; fem. acc. sg. · also masc. acc. sg. (the same form serves both genders for this adjective): ἀπείρονα πόντον ’boundless sea’
ἀπόπροθεν: ἀπόπροθεν — from afar, far off; adv.
ἀρήτη: Ἀρήτη — Arete, queen of the Phaeacians (name from ἀρητός ’prayed for’); fem. nom. sg. · also fem. voc. sg., address: ’Arete!’
ἀργαλέον: ἀργαλέος — hard, difficult, troublesome; neut. nom. sg., impersonal predicate governing an inf. · also neut. acc. sg. agreeing with a noun: ’grievous, hard’ (δεινόν τ’ ἀργαλέον τε, of λαῖτμα)
ἀργῆτι: ἀργής — bright, vivid white, gleaming; masc. dat. sg., of the lightning-flash (distinct root from ἀργός)
ἀσπαστὸν: ἀσπαστός — welcome; adj., neut. nom. sg., predicate: ’appeared welcome’
ἀχνύμενός: ἄχνυμαι — grieve, be distressed; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’grieved (though I am)’
ἁδινὰ: ἁδινός — close-packed, thronging, in a mass; neut. acc. pl.
ἁλὶ: ἅλς — sea, salt water; fem. dat. sg.
ἂν: ἄν — modal particle marking contingency (with subj. = future contingency, with opt. = potential) · also with a secondary indicative (impf./aor.) marking an unreal, contrary-to-fact conclusion: ’would’ (οὐκ ἂν ... ἀγόρευες ’you would not be speaking’) · also = ἀνά (preposition/preverb ’up’) in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἂν … βαῖνε = ἀνέβαινε, ἂν … βάντες = ἀναβάντες)
ἄλλοι: ἄλλος — other, another; masc. nom. pl.
ἄρα: ἄρα — so, as it turned out, then; inferential particle
ἄριστος: ἀγαθός — good; superlative ἄριστος ’best’; adj., masc. nom. sg.
ἄρουραν: ἄρουρα — tilled land, plowland, earth; acc. sg.
ἄσβεστον: ἄσβεστος — unquenchable, inextinguishable (ἀ- + σβέννυμι); adj., neut. nom./acc. sg. (ἄσβεστον κλέος ’fame unquenchable’)
ἄτερ: ἄτερ — without, apart from; prep. + gen.
ἄτλαντος: Ἄτλας — Atlas, the Titan who holds the pillars of sky and sea; gen. sg.
ἅ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’what things’
ἅλα: ἅλς — sea, salt sea; fem. acc. sg.
ἅπαντα: ἅπας — all, the whole of; masc. acc. sg. · also neut. nom./acc. pl., subject or object of a verb: ’all things’ (τελευτηθῆναι ἅπαντα ’that all things were fulfilled’)
ἐγώ: ἐγώ — I; nom. sg. (accented ἐγώ before the enclitic τοι that follows)
ἐείσατο: εἴδομαι — seem, appear; aor. 3 sg. ἐείσατο, unaugmented: ’seemed’
ἐθέλων: ἐθέλω — wish, be willing; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ‘willing’
ἐικυῖα: ἔοικα — be like, resemble; perf. part. fem. nom. sg., + dat.: ’likened to, having the appearance of’
ἐκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as adverb or preverb in tmesis, no case expressed: ’out’ (ἐκ δ’ ἔβαν ’and out they stepped’)
ἐκέασσε: κεάζω — split, shatter; aor. 3 sg., epic σσ (= Attic ἐκέασε): ’shattered’
ἐκέλευε: κελεύω — bid, command, urge; impf. 3 sg.: ’kept bidding’
ἐκέλευσεν: κελεύω — command, order, bid; aor. 3 sg.
ἐκβαίνοντα: ἐκβαίνω — step out, disembark; pres. part. acc. sg. masc., agreeing with an understood ’me’ (μ’ ἐκβαίνοντα)
ἐμή: ἐμός — my, mine; fem. nom. sg.
ἐμβαλέειν: ἐμβάλλω — throw in, cast upon; aor. inf. act., epic -έειν (= Attic ἐμβαλεῖν): ’to throw on’
ἐμὴν: ἐμός — my, mine; fem. acc. sg.
ἐμὸν: ἐμός — my, mine; masc./neut. acc. sg.
ἐμὸς: ἐμός — my, mine; masc. nom. sg.
ἐν: ἐν — in, on, among; + dat.; also used as an adverb, ’in it, there’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐν … βάλῃ = ἐμβάλῃ ’cast in’; ἐν … χεῦον = ἔγχεον ’pour in’)
ἐναίσιμον: ἐναίσιμος — fitting, in due measure; neut. acc. sg.
ἐνθέμεναι: ἐντίθημι — put in, place in; aor. inf. act., epic -έμεναι (= Attic ἐνθεῖναι): ’to put in’
ἐνοσίχθων: ἐνοσίχθων — earth-shaker, epithet of Poseidon (from ἔνοσις ’shaking’ + χθών ’earth’); nom. sg.
ἐνόησα: νοέω — perceive, catch sight of, notice; aor. 1 sg., augmented
ἐνόησε: νοέω — perceive, think, devise; aor. 3 sg.
ἐνὶ: ἐν (epic ἐνί) — in, on, among; + dat. · also adverb or preverb, no case: ’therein’ (ἔνθ’ ἐνὶ πέπλοι ... βεβλήατο ’therein coverlets were laid’)
ἐπ: ἐπί (elided ἐπ’) — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐπ’ … χεῦε = ἐπέχευε ‘poured upon’)
ἐπέεσσιν: ἔπος — word; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσι(ν)
ἐπέλασσε: πελάζω — bring near, drive to; aor. 3 sg.: ‘drove’
ἐπὶ: ἐπί — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as adverb, no case expressed: ’to it, over it; besides’ (θεοὶ δ’ ἐπὶ μάρτυροι ’witnesses to it’; ἐπὶ κτέρεα κτερεΐξαι ’besides’) · also + dat., ’beyond, over and above, more than’ (ἐπὶ γαστέρι κύντερον ’more shameless than the belly’)
ἐρέω: ἐρέω — say, tell, declare; fut. 1 sg. (epic fut. of εἶπον, = Attic ἐρῶ); in tmesis with ἐκ, ἐξερέω ’speak out plainly’
ἐριδούπῳ: ἐρίδουπος — loud-echoing, loud-thundering (ἐρι- + δοῦπος ’thud, din’); masc./fem./neut. dat. sg.
ἐς: εἰς (epic ἐς) — into, to; + acc. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb with no case expressed (ἐς … ἦλθον = εἰσῆλθον ’came in’)
ἐσθλοὶ: ἐσθλός — good, noble, brave; masc. nom. pl.
ἐσθλοῦ: ἐσθλός — good, noble; masc. gen. sg.
ἐσσι: εἰμί — be; pres. 2 sg., epic (= Attic εἶ)
ἐστίν: εἰμί — be; pres. 3 sg., ν-movable form
ἐυπλόκαμος: ἐϋπλόκαμος — fair-tressed, with fine hair; fem. nom. sg. (Calypso’s standing epithet) · also used of Demeter (5.125), so not unique to Calypso despite the parenthetical above
ἐφάνη: φαίνω — show; aor. pass. 3 sg., augmented (beside unaugmented φάνη): ’appeared’
ἐφύπερθε: ἐφύπερθε — over the top, above, on top of; adv.
ἐχέμεν: ἔχω — have, hold; pres. inf. act., epic -έμεν (= Attic ἔχειν), used as an imperative: ’hold on!’
ἐὺ: ἐΰ — well (Attic εὖ, printed without a diaeresis); adv.
ἐὼν: εἰμί — be; pres. part. masc. nom. sg., epic (= Attic ὤν)
ἑλὼν: αἱρέω — take, seize, grasp; aor. act. part. masc. nom. sg. (ἑλών): ’having seized’
ἑπτάετες: ἑπτάετες — for seven years; adv. (acc. of duration, ἑπτά + ἔτος)
ἑπτὰ: ἑπτά — seven; numeral, indecl. (ἑπτὰ καὶ δέκα ’seventeen’)
ἑταῖροι: ἑταῖρος — companion, comrade; masc. nom. pl.
ἔην: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἦν)
ἔκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; prep. + gen., placed after its pronoun with anastrophe: τοῦ ... ἔκ = ἐκ τοῦ ’from him’ · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἔκ … ὀνόμαζε = ἐξωνόμαζε ’called by name’)
ἔλσας: εἴλω — hem in, pin down, confine; aor. part. act. masc. nom. sg.: ’having pinned down’
ἔμελλον: μέλλω — be about to, be destined to; impf. 3 pl.
ἔμμεναι: εἰμί — be; pres. inf., epic (= Attic εἶναι)
ἔνθ: ἔνθα (elided ἔνθ’) — there, then; adverb of place or time
ἔνθα: ἔνθα — there, then; adverb of place or time · also used relatively, continuing a clause: ’where’ (ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’)
ἔπειθεν: πείθω — persuade, deceive; impf. 3 sg., augmented
ἔπεσον: πίπτω — fall; aor. 1 sg. or 3 pl., augmented (unaugmented πέσον); with σύν in tmesis, σὺν … ἔπεσον = συνέπεσον ’fell together, clashed’
ἔπος: ἔπος — word, speech, thing said; neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἔς: εἰς (epic ἐς) — into, to; prep. + acc.
ἔστ: εἰμί — be; pres. 3 sg., elided (ἔστ’ = ἔστι)
ἔφατ: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid., augmented, elided (ἔφατ’ = ἔφατο)
ἔχουσαι: ἔχω — have, hold; pres. part. fem. nom. pl.: ’holding’
ἕπεσθαι: ἕπομαι — follow, accompany, go with; pres. inf.: ’to go with, accompany’
ἕσασθαι: ἕννυμι — clothe, put on; aor. inf. mid.: ’to wear, put on (for oneself)’
ἠῶ: ἠώς (Attic ἕως) — dawn; acc. sg., accusative of extent: ’on into the dawn’
ἡ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. nom. sg.: ’she’
ἡδύ: ἡδύς — sweet, pleasant; neut. acc. sg., attributive
ἡμέτερον: ἡμέτερος — our, ours; neut. acc. sg.
ἢ: ἤ — or; disjunctive conj. (epic ἠέ/ἤ) · also ’than’ after a comparative: κρεῖσσον … ἢ ὅτε ’better than when’
ἤγαγε: ἄγω — lead, bring; aor. 3 sg., augmented: ’led, brought’
ἤματα: ἦμαρ — day; neut. acc. pl., acc. of time: ’all the days, every day’
ἤματι: ἦμαρ — day; neut. dat. sg., epic ἤματι
ἥ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. sg. · also ὁ, ἡ, τό (personal/demonstrative pronoun): she; fem. nom. sg. (ἥ γε ’she indeed’, of the ship)
ἥρως: ἥρως — hero, man of standing; masc. nom. sg. · also used as a vocative in direct address, inserted mid-sentence (ἥρως, εἴρεσθαι δέ ’and ask, hero that you are’), distinct from its use as a narrative title ’the hero’
ἦ: ἦ — truly, verily; affirming particle · also interrogative particle introducing an earnest question · also = ἤ ’or’, in the correlative ἠέ … ἦ ’whether … or’ · also ἠμί — say, speak; unaugmented aor./impf. 3 sg. (= ἔφη), closing or introducing direct speech: ’he/she said’ (ἦ ῥα ’so he said’)
ἦγον: ἄγω — lead, bring, drive; impf. 3 pl.
ἦλθεν: ἔρχομαι — come, go; aor. 3 sg., augmented: ’came’
ἦλθον: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. 3 pl.: ’they came’ · also aor. 1 sg. (the same ending serves both persons): ’I have come’
ἦμαρ: ἦμαρ — day (epic for ἡμέρα); neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἧος: ἧος — as long as, while; temporal conj., epic (= Attic ἕως) · also ’until’, and by extension ’so that’, introducing a purpose clause with the optative after a past main verb (ἧος … παύσειε ’so that it might stop her weeping’) · also plain temporal ’until’, with the indicative marking a definite past terminus: ἧος ... κατέπεφνεν ’until Artemis slew him’
ἴσαν: εἶμι — go, come; impf. 3 pl., epic: ’used to go, come’ · also as a simple narrative past, ’went’ (μνηστῆρες … ἴσαν ’the suitors went’), not necessarily iterative · also οἶδα — know; unaugmented plup. 3 pl. with impf. sense, epic (= Attic ᾔδεσαν): ’they knew’ (τὰ δ’ οὐκ ἴσαν ’they did not know’)
ἵκηαι: ἱκνέομαι — come, arrive, reach; aor. subj. 2 sg. mid.: ’you may reach’
ὀδυσσεύς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, the poem’s hero; nom. sg.
ὀδυσσεὺς: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus, the poem’s hero; nom. sg.
ὀδυσῆα: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; acc. sg. (single-σ metrical variant of Ὀδυσσῆα)
ὀκτωκαιδεκάτῃ: ὀκτωκαιδέκατος — eighteenth; fem. dat. sg. (sc. ἡμέρῃ), ’on the eighteenth (day)’
ὀνόμαζεν: ὀνομάζω — call by name, name; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= Attic ὠνόμαζε); with ἐκ in tmesis (ἔκ … ὀνόμαζεν) ’called by name’
ὀπίσσω: ὀπίσσω — behind; in Homer also ’hereafter, in time to come’; adv.
ὁ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. sg.
ὄρεα: ὄρος — mountain; neut. nom./acc. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic ὄρη)
ὄφρ: ὄφρα (elided ὄφρ’) — so that, in order that; epic (= Attic ἵνα); + subj. · also temporal, ’as long as, while’ + indicative (ὄφρ’ ἔτι κεῖνος ἀνὴρ ἐπιδήμιος ἦεν ’as long as that man was still at home’) · also ’while’ + ἄν and subj. · also temporal ’until’ + indicative (ὄφρ’ ἵκετ’ Ἀρήτην ’until he came to Arete’)
ὄφρα: ὄφρα — so that, in order that; epic (= Attic ἵνα); + subj. · also temporal, ’until’, + indic. (ὄφρα ... βάλε): marking the point an action ceases · also temporal + subj. with κε, correlative with τόφρα: ’as long as, until’ (ὄφρα κε κείνη τοῦτον ἔχῃ νόον ’for as long as she holds this purpose’) · also + opt. in a purpose clause after a secondary-sequence verb: ὄφρα ... ἕλοις/ἵκοιο ’so that you might take/arrive’
ὅ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg.; with γε: ’he’ · also relative, masc. nom. sg., accented before an enclitic: ’who’ (ὅ κε ... ἐφείη) · also = ὅτι ’that’; εἰς ὅ ’until’ · also relative, neut. nom./acc. sg.: ’which’ (ὅ οἱ πέρι δῶκεν Ἀθήνη ’which Athena gave her beyond others’) · also masc. nom. sg. pronoun ’he’ without γε, accented before an enclitic (ὅ σφιν ’he … to them’)
ὅς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.)
ὅσα: ὅσος — as much/many as; neut. acc. pl.: ’all that, as much as’
ὅσσον: ὅσος (epic ὅσσος) — as much/great as; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially, correlative with τόσσον: ’as far as’
ὅτε: ὅτε — when; temporal conjunction · also ’since, now that’ (ὅτε πρότερός γε πύθοιτο ’since he learned of it first’) · also with the optative, hypothetical/conditional: ’if ever, whenever’ (ὅτε ... ἵκοι ’if ever such need should come upon me’) · also with the subjunctive, general: ’whenever’ (ὅτε στείχῃσ’ ἀνὰ ἄστυ ’whenever she goes through the town’)
ὑπ: ὑπό (elided ὑπ’) — under, beneath; prep. + gen.; also + acc., ’under, up under’ · also of agent with a verb of dying, ‘by, at the hands of’ + gen. (ὤλεθ’ ὑπ’ Αἰγίσθοιο ‘perished by Aegisthus’) · also + dat., ’under, beneath’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb, no case governed: οὓς ὑπ’ Ὀδυσσεὺς δύσετ’ = ὑπεδύσετο ’underneath which Odysseus sank down’
ὑψηλοῖο: ὑψηλός — high, lofty; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -οῦ)
ὕδωρ: ὕδωρ — water; neut. acc. sg. · also nom. sg. (identical neut. form), subject of a verb (ἄνεμός τε καὶ ὕδωρ ‘wind and current’)
ὕπνῳ: ὕπνος — sleep; masc. dat. sg. (ὕπνῳ γλυκερῷ ’sweet sleep’)
ὠγυγίην: Ὠγυγίη — Ogygia, the island of Calypso; acc. sg.
ὡς: ὡς — as, how, that, when; with the optative introduces a wish: ’so may…’ (unaccented; accented ὥς / ὣς is ’thus’) · also ὡς + unaugmented ὄφελον + inf., an unfulfillable wish: ’would that...’ · also ὡς + opt., a purpose clause (= ἵνα): ’so that’ (ὡς τὸν χόλον ἐξακέσαιτο ’so that he might appease the anger’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. + inf.: ’how (good, etc.) it is to...’ (ὡς ἀγαθὸν ... λιπέσθαι ’how good a thing it is to be left behind’) · also plain ὡς + indic., ’as’ (ὡς σὺ κελεύεις ’as you command’) or ’how’ in an indirect question (ὡς ἐπὶ πόντον ἐλεύσομαι ’how I shall come upon the sea’) · also ὡς ἄν + subj., a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὡς ἂν μὴ κλαίουσα κατὰ χρόα καλὸν ἰάπτῃς ’so that you might not mar your fair skin with weeping’) · also ὡς δ’ ὅτε introducing an epic simile, ’as when’, its clause taking indic. or ἄν/κε + subj. for a general case: ὡς δ’ ὅτ’ ἂν ... φανήῃ ’as when ... should appear’ · also comparative ’like’, placed after the noun it compares (ἀνέμου ὡς πνοιή ’like a blast of wind’) · also ὡς εἰ ’as if, like’ (ὡς εἰ πτερὸν ἠὲ νόημα ’as if a wing or a thought’)
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως) · also postpositive after its noun (anastrophe), = comparative ὡς ’as, like’: ὄρνις δ’ ὥς ’like a bird’
ῥήγεα: ῥῆγος — rug, coverlet (laid on a bed); neut. nom./acc. pl.
